iut_type: Distinguishing the different name/identity fields in derivative-model addition registration documents -- Username, Name (signature), and Listing Owner
customer_question: Which name should I enter in the 'Listing Owner' field of the derivative-model addition document -- is it just my own name (Hirotaka Kotake)? Also, there are two types of registered names in this form -- which one is needed here?
question_variants: Does 'Listing Owner' refer to the company name, the account holder's name, or something else?
Should the signature field use my login Username (nickname) or my real Name?
actual_issue: While filling out the derivative-model addition registration document, the customer encountered multiple distinct-looking name/identity fields (Username, a signature 'Name' field, and 'Listing Owner') and was unsure which value belonged in which field.
plain_english_explanation: These registration documents distinguish between three different identity concepts that can easily be confused: (1) Username is purely a login-account identifier and can be any nickname the account holder chose when registering the account -- it has no requirement to be a real name; (2) the document's signature field requires the person's actual real Name, not their Username/nickname; (3) Listing Owner refers specifically to the account registration name of whoever is logged in when reaching the relevant registration screen -- so if the customer's own account (registered under 'Hirotaka Kotake') was used to reach that screen, 'Hirotaka Kotake' is the correct value to enter as the Listing Owner.
consultant_answer: Listing Owner refers to the account registration name of whoever logged in to reach this screen -- since you logged in under your own account, 'Hirotaka Kotake' is correct there. Separately, Username is just a login-account nickname and can be anything; please use your actual Name in the document's signature field, not the Username.
decision_logic: When a registration or addition document contains multiple distinct name-like fields, clarify each field's specific meaning explicitly -- Username is an arbitrary login nickname, the signature field requires the person's actual legal name, and Listing Owner is whichever account's registration name was used to log in and reach that particular screen -- rather than assuming the customer will infer the correct mapping.
final_recommendation: When sending a registration document with multiple name-like fields to a customer for completion, proactively annotate or explain what each field expects (login nickname vs. real name vs. logged-in account's registration name) to avoid back-and-forth clarification questions.
risk_if_done_wrong: Entering the wrong value in a given name field (e.g., a login nickname in the signature field, or the wrong account's name as Listing Owner) could create inconsistencies in the registration record that might need later correction.
